rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for something unclear, indistinct, or lacking a sharp outline.

example.english: This photo is too vague for me to make out clearly.
example.traditional: 呢張相太模糊，我睇唔清楚。
example.jyutping: ne1 zoeng1 soeng2 taai3 mou4 wu4 ngo5 tai2 m4 cing1 co2

rows.note: Use this when a statement, term, or meaning is unclear because it is expressed ambiguously.

example.english: You are being vague, so I do not know what you mean.
example.traditional: 你講得咁含糊，我唔知你想點。
example.jyutping: nei5 gong2 dak1 gam3 ham4 wu4 ngo5 m4 zi1 nei5 soeng2 dim2

rows.note: Use this for a faint, barely conscious, or indistinct feeling rather than an unclear statement.

example.english: I had a vague feeling that someone was calling me.
example.traditional: 我隱隱約約覺得有人叫我。
example.jyutping: ngo5 jan2 jan2 joek3 joek3 gok3 dak1 jau5 jan4 giu3 ngo5

rows.note: Use this for someone who is dazed or mentally muddled, especially after an accident or injury.

example.english: After bumping his head, he was completely vague about what had happened.
example.traditional: 佢撞親個頭之後，成個人懵查查咁。
example.jyutping: keoi5 zong6 can1 go3 tau4 zi1 hau6 seng4 go3 jan4 mung2 caa4 caa4 gam2
